title: KappaHealth deploy ops cookbook and open edges
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a tactical 'cookbook' created after the standup on 2026-09-15 for the KappaHealth on-prem/VPC deployment. It captures observed install exceptions, triage notes, and short-term runbook edits we should apply to reduce the same re-occurring blockers across future customers.

Meeting snapshot:
- When: 2026-09-15 09:30 PT
- Attendees: Maya Chen (lead), Evan Morales (networks), Priya Nair (field eng), Jonah Park (security), Customer: KappaHealth infra (S. Iyengar, T. Lowe)
- Motivation: unblock production VPC peering and finalize HSM/KMS integration for go-live next Tue 2026-09-21

Summary of current state:
- Control plane deployed to customer's VPC and initial agent installed on three on-prem nodes.
- Data plane attempts fail intermittently; observed high connection churn from reds-rt-01 (our BGP speaker) to customer transit router.
- Customer reports degraded API traffic through their firewall; internal logs show fragmented TLS handshakes reaching our edge.
- KMS integration: key wrap test fails with 502 from customer HSM proxy when we attempt remote_sign.

Primary blockers (root-cause notes):
1) MTU mismatch / fragmentation between cloud transit and on-prem DMZ
   - Symptom: TLS ClientHello split into fragments, causing handshake timeouts.
   - Evidence: tcpdump on customer edge shows MSS 1400, our side expects 1500.
   - Immediate mitigation: prefer TCP MSS clamping on peering (customer to add iptables mss clamp at egress).

2) BGP flap triggered by route-reflect loop on customer's edge equipment
   - Symptom: bgp session resets every ~7 minutes; our session goes into Active briefly then recovers.
   - Evidence: bgp dumps show AS path change when Kappa's new transit appliance reboots.
   - Notes: hardware vendor firmware 3.2.1 known issue; customer scheduled patch but timeline uncertain.

3) HSM proxy rejecting our SRP cipher suites behind corporate TLS terminator
   - Symptom: 502 on remote_sign, error contains 'unexpected EOF' or 'tls: received unexpected message'.
   - Evidence: curl from our test container with --tlsv1.3 works to admin endpoint, but HSM proxy rewrites headers and injects a corporate proxy (BlueGate) causing handshake mismatch.
   - Temporary workaround: route KMS traffic through customer secure tunnel straight into HSM DMZ (bypass proxy), pending security approval.

Operational action items (owners + due dates):
- Evan: Add MSS clamp rule to red-team peering doc and request customer to mirror on their egress (due 2026-09-16).
- Priya: Run a controlled mtudisc test (path-mtu-discovery) with customer network team and post pcap to JIRA PD-4821 (due 2026-09-16).
- Jonah: Prepare exception request template for security to allow KMS tunnel bypass through specific IPs/subnets; include ACL snippet (due 2026-09-17).
- Maya: Draft runbook edits (section: 'VPC peering - MTU & BGP flaps') and add checklist for HSM integration steps (due 2026-09-17).
- Customer action (S. Iyengar): confirm firmware patch schedule with vendor and provide firm date (expected 2026-09-20).

Triage notes / commands tried so far (for runbook insertion):
- tcpdump on host: sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/kappa-handshake.pcap 'tcp port 443 and (tcp[13] & 2 != 0)'
- check BGP: vtysh -c 'show bgp summary' -> observe frequent 4xx/Active + last reset reason 'Neighbor Closed the session'.
- mtudisc test: ping -M do -s 1472 <customer-addr> -> fails; success at 1400
- KMS curl test: curl -v --tlsv1.3 https://hsm-proxy.kappa.example.com/health -> 502 with truncated body

Proposed short-term runbook edits (explicit paragraphs to paste into Confluence):
- Add 'MTU sanity' step to pre-install checklist: confirm end-to-end MTU >= 1500 or document required MSS clamp rule. Provide sample iptables command: iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
- Add BGP resilience recommendations: set 'bgp dampening' off for peering sessions with customer edge during install window; record neighbor session monitoring cadence (1m intervals). Document fallback policy: if session flaps > 5x in 30m, revert to static routing for control-plane traffic and open PD ticket for hardware vendor escalation.
- KMS/HSM guidance: require an explicit 'bypass tunnel' acceptance form from customer's security team including allowed source IP ranges and duration. Provide sample OpenVPN tunnel configuration and IP ACL snippet for quick provisioning.

Customer communication draft (to send after runbook update):
Hi Suneel / Team,

Thanks again for the morning call. We made three changes we want to align on before we continue: (1) we suggest enabling MSS clamping on your egress (we'll provide the exact iptables command), (2) for the install window please confirm whether you can temporarily accept a bypassed KMS tunnel, and (3) confirm vendor firmware patch ETA for the transit appliance. We can coordinate a short maintenance window Friday 2026-09-17 03:00–04:00 UTC for the mtudisc and BGP stabilization tests.

Open questions / risks:
- If firmware patch slips past 2026-09-20, we risk repeated 7-minute control-plane blips affecting KV cache priming (higher client-side 5xx rates).
- Customer security may not approve bypass quickly; if denial occurs, our alternative is to do an in-proxy TLS handshake shim (significant dev effort) which will delay go-live by 2–3 sprints.

Notes for product/infra teams (internal):
- Consider adding an automated MTU check to the onboarding agent that reports path MTU to the control plane during install. This could auto-surface before we create peering.
- Add a flag to deployment manifests to mark KMS endpoints requiring 'direct_peer' in routing table, so operators can toggle proxy-bypass quickly.

Follow-ups / next meetings:
- Daily standup 2026-09-16 09:30 PT (15m) to confirm mitigations progress.
- Technical deep-dive with Kappa security and vendor rep (firmware) scheduled 2026-09-16 16:00 PT.

Appendix: quick references
- Relevant JIRA: PD-4821 (Kappa MTU/BGP), PD-4889 (KMS proxy failure)
- Slack threads: #kappa-install (link pinned messages), #field-installs-ops
- Contact: S. Iyengar (KappaHead, infra lead)

End of notes.
